"Below are questions proposed for a research problem, each with the reframing behind it. Classify each one.
kind: \"reframe\" if it changes what is computed, measured or ordered so that more compute buys something it did not before; \"copies\" if it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; \"other\" otherwise.
meets_criterion: \"yes\" or \"no\" for this criterion: It removes a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on (time steps, chain iterations or solver iterations), so that those steps are computed at the same time. Running independent copies side by side, or splitting each single step across GPUs, does not count.
Give for each a quote from the proposal and a reason of at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Problem:
Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models for river catchments, which needs long MCMC chains.
Proposals: [{\"index\":1,\"title\":\"Split each step\",\"summary\":\"Split each daily time step's 2 million grid cells across 8 GPUs with domain decomposition, exchanging halos every step.\"},{\"index\":2,\"title\":\"Whole-chain Newton\",\"summary\":\"Guess all 10,000 states of one MCMC chain at once, then correct every state in parallel with Newton iterations until the chain matches the sequential one.\"},{\"index\":3,\"title\":\"Scan over days\",\"summary\":\"Each day's update of the linear reservoir model is an affine map, so compute all 36,500 days at once with a parallel prefix scan instead of the time loop.\"},{\"index\":4,\"title\":\"Many chains\",\"summary\":\"Run 4,096 independent MCMC chains side by side on the GPU, one per starting point, and pool their samples.\"}]

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"items\"],\"properties\":{\"items\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"index\",\"kind\",\"meets_criterion\",\"quote\",\"reason\"],\"properties\":{\"index\":{\"type\":\"integer\"},\"kind\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"enum\":[\"reframe\",\"copies\",\"other\"]},\"meets_criterion\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"enum\":[\"yes\",\"no\",\"NA\"]},\"quote\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"reason\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"

Let me analyze each proposal.

The problem: Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models for river catchments, needs long MCMC chains.

Criterion: It removes a step-after-step dependency that one answer waits on (time steps, chain iterations or solver iterations), so that those steps are computed at the same time. Running independent copies side by side, or splitting each single step across GPUs, does not count.

Kind: "reframe" if it changes what is computed, measured or ordered so that more compute buys something it did not before; "copies" if it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; "other" otherwise.

Proposal 1: "Split each daily time step's 2 million grid cells across 8 GPUs with domain decomposition, exchanging halos every step." — This splits each single step across GPUs. That's explicitly excluded from meeting the criterion. What kind? It's not running the same computation more times or side by side independent copies... Actually it is running the same computation but parallelizing within each step across spatial domain. Hmm, "copies" is defined as "it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side". Splitting grid cells across GPUs is running the same computation on more items side by side? It's parallelizing spatially within a step. The time loop remains. So it doesn't remove the step dependency. Kind: this is data parallelism within a step — I'd call it "copies" (running the same computation on more items, side by side) — or "other". The definition of copies: "only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side". Splitting grid cells across 8 GPUs is running the same computation side by side on subsets of items. So kind = "copies". meets_criterion = "no" (explicitly: splitting each single step across GPUs does not count).

Proposal 2: "Guess all 10,000 states of one MCMC chain at once, then correct every state in parallel with Newton iterations until the chain matches the sequential one." — This is a reframe: changes what is computed (parallel-in-time / Picard/Newton iteration over whole chain) so more compute buys something (removes chain iteration dependency). It removes the step-after-step dependency of MCMC chain iterations — all states computed at once. Kind = "reframe". meets_criterion = "yes". Quote: "Guess all 10,000 states of one MCMC chain at once, then correct every state in parallel with Newton iterations until the chain matches the sequential one." Reason: turns sequential chain into one parallel Newton correction over all states, removing step dependency.

Proposal 3: "Each day's update of the linear reservoir model is an affine map, so compute all 36,500 days at once with a parallel prefix scan instead of the time loop." — Parallel prefix scan over time steps removes time-step dependency. Kind = "reframe". meets_criterion = "yes". Reason: prefix scan computes all days simultaneously, removing the day-to-day time-step dependency.

Proposal 4: "Run 4,096 independent MCMC chains side by side on the GPU, one per starting point, and pool their samples." — Independent copies side by side. Kind = "copies". meets_criterion = "no" (running independent copies side by side does not count).

For proposal 1, meets_criterion = "no" since splitting each single step across GPUs does not count. Kind: hmm. Is it "copies" or "other"? The kind taxonomy: "reframe" if changes what is computed/measured/ordered so more compute buys something new; "copies" if only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; "other" otherwise. Domain decomposition splits a step's grid cells across GPUs — it runs the same computation on more items side by side (data parallelism). So "copies" fits. Alternatively "other" since it's not running more times nor more items — it's the same items divided. But "side by side" covers spatial parallelism within a step. I'd say "copies". Actually more carefully: "runs the same computation ... on more items, or side by side" — splitting 2M grid cells across 8 GPUs is running the same computation on the same items but distributed. The spirit: it's pure data/task parallelism that doesn't restructure. Both "copies" and "other" could arguably fit; "copies" seems the intended classification for spatial domain decomposition since it doesn't change what's computed and doesn't remove dependencies. The schema note says independent copies or splitting each step across GPUs does not count for criterion. For kind, domain decomposition is basically running parts of the same computation side by side. I'll go with "copies".

meets_criterion for proposal 1: "no".

Reasons (≤25 words):
1: "Splits work within each time step across GPUs; the time-step dependency remains, and splitting single steps does not count."
2: "Replaces sequential chain steps with simultaneous guesses corrected in parallel; removes chain-iteration dependency so more compute shortens the chain."
3: "Prefix scan computes all days simultaneously, removing the time-step dependency of the reservoir update loop."
4: "Independent chains side by side only; each chain still runs step-after-step, and parallel copies do not count."

Quotes: use exact text from summary.

{"items":[{"index":1,"kind":"copies","meets_criterion":"no","quote":"Split each daily time step's 2 million grid cells across 8 GPUs with domain decomposition, exchanging halos every step.","reason":"Splits work within each time step across GPUs; the step-after-step time dependency remains, and splitting single steps does not count."},{"index":2,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"yes","quote":"Guess all 10,000 states of one MCMC chain at once, then correct every state in parallel with Newton iterations until the chain matches the sequential one.","reason":"Replaces sequential chain steps with simultaneous guesses corrected by parallel Newton iterations, removing the chain-iteration dependency entirely."},{"index":3,"kind":"reframe","meets_criterion":"yes","quote":"Each day's update of the linear reservoir model is an affine map, so compute all 36,500 days at once with a parallel prefix scan instead of the time loop.","reason":"Parallel prefix scan computes all daily updates simultaneously, removing the time-step dependency of the sequential loop."},{"index":4,"kind":"copies","meets_criterion":"no","quote":"Run 4,096 independent MCMC chains side by side on the GPU, one per starting point, and pool their samples.","reason":"Only runs independent chains side by side; each chain still waits on its own steps, and parallel copies do not count."}]}
